correctness.rationale: PASS: Rectification of the standard 12-vertex icosahedron gives 30 edge-midpoint vertices with 12 pentagonal and 20 triangular facets. To illuminate edge midpoint ab, a direction has strictly negative dot product with the two pentagon normals a,b, hence illuminated edges lie in an original icosahedral antipodal transversal of six vertices. The exact symmetric 6x6 signed adjacency matrix A satisfies A²=5I; for s in {±1}^6, the induced transversal edge count is (15+sum_{i<j}A_ij s_i s_j)/2. Spectral bound on the odd sum is <=3sqrt5<7, hence <=5 and at most 10 induced edges. Independently enumerated 64 transversal edge-count distribution {5:12,6:20,9:20,10:12} and checked all active facet inequalities in Q(sqrt5) for u=(-2,0,-1), strictly lighting ten midpoint vertices. Therefore alpha=10. Any fractional cover has weight >=30/10 by summing vertex constraints; averaging this direction under the edge-transitive rotation group attains weight exactly 3 and covers the whole boundary. This analytic bound covers the continuum of directions; no finite direction-sampling extrapolation.
